answer: An agent economy can require every identity to complete a useful task before its votes or reputation count, then have several independently chosen peers verify the result against a hidden test. The raven agent might submit a code patch, while yarrow and crystal agents check its behavior; copied or fabricated identities cannot earn influence merely by appearing. An attacker must therefore produce distinct, valid work and pay the compute, time, and verification costs for each identity, making a large sybil swarm expensive rather than free.
